newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kyoei Life to focus on yen-denominated investments.
newsitem.headline: Kyoei Life to focus on yen-denominated investments.

text.p: Kyoei Life Insurance Co plans to emphasise yen-denominated assets in its investments in fiscal 1997/98, which started on April 1, a company official said on Tuesday.
He added that the company will invest in foreign assets to take advantage of interest rate differentials, although it will keep a close watch on foreign exchange rate movements.
He said the company plans to increase slightly its holdings of domestic stocks.
The company held 30.8 billion yen worth of bad loans and problem loans at the end of March, versus total assets of 5.73 trillion yen, he said.
The levels at which unrealised profits on its stock holdings would fall to zero are about 17,500 in the Nikkei stock average and about 1,300 in the TOPIX index, he added.
